description.en: Barbells and racks, a full dumbbell rack, cables and the usual machines.
A barbell with plates, a power rack with a pull-up bar, an adjustable bench and adjustable dumbbells.
Adjustable dumbbells and an adjustable bench.
A pull-up bar, dip bars, rings and resistance bands.
Light to medium dumbbells, an adjustable bench, a cable station and cardio machines.
Start with nothing selected and add your own equipment.

cues.en: Brace before you unrack and keep the bar over mid-foot.
Sit down between your hips until your hip crease is below the knee.
Let your knees travel forward over your toes as far as your depth needs.
Drive up with intent, chest and hips rising together.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and keep your feet planted.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest, elbows slightly tucked.
Touch the chest every rep; for competition practice, hold it still before you press.
Press the bar up and slightly back until your elbows lock out.
Start with the bar over mid-foot and your shins close to it.
Brace, pull the slack out of the bar, then push the floor away.
Keep the bar close and finish with hips and knees locked out together.
Lower the bar under control along the same path, then reset before the next rep.
Take a wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar inside your legs.
Push your knees out over your toes and bring your hips close to the bar.
Brace and spread the floor with your feet as the bar leaves the ground.
Lock out by squeezing your hips through without leaning back.
Squat to your usual competition depth, then hold still for two seconds.
Stay braced and tight in the hole; do not relax onto your knees or hips.
Drive out of the pause without a bounce, keeping the bar over mid-foot.
Rest the bar on your front delts with high elbows and a relaxed grip.
Keep your torso upright and sit straight down as deep as you can stay braced.
Lead the drive up with your elbows so the bar does not roll forward.
Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest.
Sit down between your heels, elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
Go as deep as you can with a neutral back, then stand up tall.
Place your feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.
Lower the sled until your knees are well bent, without your lower back lifting off the pad.
Press through your whole foot and stop just short of locking your knees.
Set up and brace exactly as you do for your competition squat.
Count four slow seconds on the way down while the bar stays over mid-foot.
Hold the bottom for one second without relaxing your brace.
Stand up with full intent once the pause is over.
Set the safety pins so the bar rests on them when you are at competition depth.
Lower under control until the bar settles on the pins, staying braced the whole time.
Drive the bar up from the dead stop without rocking or bouncing it off the pins.
Rest the padded yoke on your upper back and hold the handles in front of you.
Keep your chest up, because the bar's forward pull tries to tip your torso over.
Squat as deep as you can stay braced, then drive your upper back up into the pads.
Set your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and sink until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Keep your lower back against the pad and press through your whole foot.
Lock the safety handles again before you step out.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before you load the bar.
Rest the bar on your upper back with your feet slightly in front of it.
Sit down until your thighs are at least parallel, heels flat on the floor.
Push the floor away and let the rails guide the bar back up.
Place a bench or box behind you at a height where your thighs are about parallel when seated.
Sit back and down under control until you touch the box, without dropping onto it.
Pause briefly while staying braced, then drive up from the box.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your toes turned slightly out.
Sit down between your heels as deep as you can while your heels stay flat.
Stand up tall; slow the descent or add a pause at the bottom once reps get easy.
Stand on a stable plate or platform about 2–5 cm high.
Set up as in your competition pull; the extra depth comes from bending your knees and hips more.
Keep your back neutral off the floor and stay over the bar longer.
Start standing with the bar in your hands and knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs with a neutral back.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually just below the knee.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall without leaning back.
Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs with knees softly bent.
Hinge at the hips and let the dumbbells travel close to your legs.
Stop when your hamstrings are fully stretched and your back is still neutral.
Squeeze your glutes to return to standing.
Stand on one leg with that knee softly bent; hold a weight in the opposite hand if you have one.
Tip forward from the hip while your free leg reaches back in line with your torso.
Keep your hips square to the floor and lower until your hamstring is fully stretched.
Rest the plates on sturdy blocks or stacked plates so the bar starts just below your knees.
Set up as you would from the floor, with the bar close and the slack pulled out.
Lock out hips and knees together, then lower the bar back onto the blocks under control.
Start the pull exactly as in your competition deadlift.
Stop when the bar is a few centimetres off the floor and hold it there for one to two seconds.
Keep your back flat and the bar against your shins during the pause.
Finish the pull from the pause in the same positions you held.
Stand in the middle of the bar with your feet about hip-width apart and grip the handles.
Bend at your hips and knees with your chest up until your arms hang straight to the handles.
Brace and push the floor away until you stand tall, then lower along the same path.
Rest the bar on your upper back as for a squat and unlock your knees slightly.
Push your hips back and let your torso tip forward with your back flat.
Go down until your hamstrings are fully stretched, usually with your torso a little above horizontal.
Drive your hips forward to stand up, and start light, because this loads your lower back hard.
Stand with the bell a step in front of you, hinge and grip it with both hands.
Hike it back between your legs, then snap your hips forward so it floats to chest height.
Let your arms only guide the bell; the power comes from your hips, not from a squat or a lift.
Hinge again as the bell comes down and keep your back flat throughout.
Stand facing away from a low pulley with the rope passing between your legs.
Hinge at the hips and let the rope draw your hands back through your legs.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, arms staying long.
Anchor a band low behind you and hold it between your legs with both hands.
Hinge back until you feel your hamstrings stretch, keeping your back flat.
Snap your hips forward against the band and finish standing tall.
Stand on the middle of a band and loop the top across your upper back.
Push your hips back with soft knees and a flat back until your torso nears horizontal.
Drive your hips forward to stand up against the band's pull.
Set up exactly as for your competition bench.
Hold the bar motionless on your chest for two to three seconds without sinking.
Keep your upper back tight through the pause, then press with full intent.
Grip the bar about shoulder-width, a hand or so narrower than your bench grip.
Keep your elbows closer to your sides as the bar comes down to the lower chest.
Press to full lockout, finishing the rep with your triceps.
Kick the dumbbells up from your knees as you lie back, then set your shoulder blades.
Lower the dumbbells beside your chest until you feel a stretch across the pecs.
Press up and slightly together without clanking the dumbbells at the top.
Set the bench to about 30–45 degrees.
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest with elbows slightly in front of the torso.
Press up over your upper chest, keeping your shoulder blades on the bench.
Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Let the handles come back until you feel a stretch, shoulders staying down.
Press out smoothly and stop just short of slamming the stack at lockout.
Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and hold a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to a fist's height above the floor with elbows angled back.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight; raise your feet to make it harder.
Set up exactly as for your competition bench press.
Lower the bar under control and stop it a finger-width or two above your chest.
Hold it there for a moment without touching, then press to lockout.
Put a flat bench in the rack and set the safety pins so the bar rests just above your chest.
Lower the bar onto the pins under control and let it settle for a moment while you stay tight.
Press from the dead stop with full intent, shoulder blades pinned back.
Lie down as for your competition bench, then straighten your legs and lift your feet just off the floor.
Keep your upper back tight without any leg drive, so your chest, shoulders and triceps do all the work.
Touch your chest and press to lockout without shifting your hips.
Set the bench to about 30–45 degrees inside the rack with the hooks at arm's length.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just below the collarbones, with your elbows slightly tucked.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench and press the bar back up over your shoulders.
Set the bench to about 30–45 degrees so the bar comes down just below your collarbones.
Lower the bar to your upper chest with your elbows slightly in front of it.
Press up along the rails without letting your shoulders roll forward.
Hook your legs under the pads and lie back with your eyes under the bar.
Lower the bar to your lower chest under control.
Press up until your elbows lock, and use a spotter or the bench's safeties when you go heavy.
Place a flat bench so the bar comes down to your lower chest.
Unhook the bar, set your shoulder blades and lower it to your chest under control.
Press up along the rails and turn the bar back onto the hooks after the last rep.
Lie on the floor with your knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
Lower until your upper arms rest lightly on the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
Press the dumbbells back up without bouncing your arms off the floor.
Set the pulley at chest height and stand facing away from it in a staggered stance.
Start with the handle beside your chest and your elbow behind your torso.
Press forward and slightly inward until your arm is straight, keeping your hips square.
Hang the rings a few centimetres off the floor and hold them with straight arms, body in one line.
Lower until your hands are beside your chest, keeping the rings close to your body.
Press up and turn the rings slightly out at the top; raise your feet to make it harder.
Place your hands on a bench, box or sturdy table a little wider than your shoulders.
Hold a straight line from head to heels and lower your chest to the edge.
Press away until your arms are straight; a lower surface makes it harder.
Place your hands close together under your chest so thumbs and index fingers form a triangle.
Lower your chest toward your hands with your elbows tracking back along your sides.
Press up to straight arms; put your hands on a bench if the full version is too hard.
Unrack the bar at collarbone height with forearms vertical and glutes squeezed.
Press straight up, moving your head back just enough for the bar to pass.
Finish with the bar over mid-foot and your head through, then lower to the collarbones.
Sit on an upright bench or stand, dumbbells at shoulder height and palms forward.
Press up until your arms are straight, letting the dumbbells drift slightly together.
Lower until the dumbbells are level with your ears or a little below.
Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in until your hips point up.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands.
Press back up; raise your feet on a box to make it harder.
Support yourself on straight arms and lean your torso slightly forward.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, or as deep as your shoulders allow.
Press back to straight arms; add weight with a dip belt when 15 reps are easy.
Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.
Lower the handles back to shoulder height under control.
Hold the bar on your front delts with a grip just outside your shoulders.
Dip a few centimetres at the knees with your torso upright, then drive up hard through your legs.
Let the leg drive start the bar and finish the press overhead with your arms.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders under control, absorbing it with your knees.
Sit tall with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders and your palms facing you.
Turn your palms forward as you press up, finishing with straight arms overhead.
Reverse the rotation on the way down to return to the start.
Set one end of the bar in the landmine and hold the loaded end at your shoulder.
Stand in a split stance or half-kneel with your ribs down and your glutes tight.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight, then lower it back to your shoulder.
Stand on the middle of the band and hold the ends at shoulder height.
Press straight up until your arms are locked, keeping your ribs down.
Lower slowly back to your shoulders; a shorter grip on the band adds tension.
Kick up into a handstand facing a wall, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Lower your head under control until it lightly touches a folded mat.
Press back up to straight arms; stay with pike push-ups until you can do several reps.
Support yourself on the rings with straight arms and the rings close to your sides.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, leaning slightly forward.
Press back up and turn the rings out a little at the top to stay steady.
Loop a band across the dip bars and rest your knees or feet on it once you are in support.
Lower with a slight forward lean until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Press up to straight arms, and switch to a lighter band as you get stronger.
Hinge forward until your torso is at about 30–45 degrees above the floor, back neutral.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, driving the elbows back past your torso.
Lower until your arms are straight without letting your torso rise.
Support yourself with one hand and knee on a bench, the other foot on the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down until your shoulder blade stretches forward.
Row the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your torso still.
Lie chest-down on a bench set to about 30 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Row both dumbbells up until your elbows pass your torso.
Keep your chest on the pad; lower until your arms are straight.
Sit tall with a slight knee bend and reach forward until your shoulder blades spread.
Pull the handle to your lower ribs while your torso stays nearly upright.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then let your arms extend fully again.
Hang under rings or a bar at hip height with your body straight and heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to your hands, keeping hips in line with shoulders and ankles.
Walk your feet forward or raise them on a box to make it harder.
Straddle the bar near its loaded end and grip it with both hands or a V-handle under the sleeve.
Hinge until your torso is at about 45 degrees or lower, back flat.
Row the plates toward your lower chest, then lower until your arms are fully straight.
Sit or stand facing a low or middle pulley and hold one handle with your arm reaching forward.
Let your shoulder blade glide forward at the start of each rep for a full stretch.
Row the handle toward your hip without twisting your torso.
Sit with your legs straight and the band looped around your feet, or anchor it at chest height.
Pull the ends toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back past your torso.
Return slowly until your arms are straight and your shoulders reach forward.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward to about 45 degrees with a flat back.
Row both dumbbells toward your hips, elbows close to your sides.
Lower until your arms hang straight while your torso stays still.
Lock your thighs under the pad and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Let the bar pull your arms fully straight at the top so your lats stretch.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Lower to a full hang on every rep; add weight with a dip belt when sets get easy.
Hang with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, keeping your chest up.
Lower all the way to straight arms before the next rep.
Loop a band over the bar and place one foot or knee in it.
Pull as in a normal pull-up, chin over the bar and a full hang at the bottom.
Switch to a lighter band as you get stronger.
Kneel or sit under a high pulley and hold one handle with your arm stretched overhead.
Pull your elbow down toward your hip without leaning away from the cable.
Let the handle rise until your lat is fully stretched before the next rep.
Anchor the band high, for example over a pull-up bar or a door, and kneel facing it.
Pull the ends down toward your shoulders, driving your elbows to your sides.
Let your arms rise back overhead slowly while the band stays taut.
Stand facing a high pulley and hold a bar or rope with straight arms at about eye level.
Hinge slightly forward and sweep your hands down to your thighs with your arms almost straight.
Let the handle rise slowly until you feel your lats stretch overhead.
Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell with both hands above your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and lower the weight in an arc behind your head until your lats stretch.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc without bending your elbows further.
Rest the top of your back foot on a bench and stand about a long stride in front of it.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is at least parallel to the floor.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot and drive up through its whole sole.
Finish all reps on one leg before you switch sides.
Take a long split stance with both feet pointing forward.
Drop your back knee toward the floor until it almost touches.
Push up through the front foot; add a backpack or a pause when reps get easy.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and take a long step forward.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, front shin close to vertical.
Push through the front foot to bring the back leg through into the next step.
Stand tall and step one foot back far enough that both knees can bend to about 90 degrees.
Lower your back knee toward the floor with most of your weight on the front foot.
Drive through the front foot to stand up again; hold dumbbells once it gets easy.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back and step into a long split stance.
Lower straight down until your back knee almost touches the floor.
Drive up through your front foot with your torso upright, and switch legs after the set.
Stand facing a sturdy bench or box about knee height with a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one whole foot on top and push through it to stand up on the box.
Do not push off the back foot, and lower yourself slowly with the working leg.
Stand on one leg and hold the other leg straight out in front of you.
Sit down on the standing leg as deep as you can control, arms forward for balance.
Stand up without letting the knee cave in; hold a door frame or sit to a bench while you learn it.
Take a wide step to the side and sit back into that hip while the other leg stays straight.
Keep both feet flat and your chest up as you lower until your inner thigh stretches.
Push off the bent leg to return to the start; hold a weight at your chest to add load.
Line up your knees with the pivot and set the pad just above your ankles.
Recline the backrest if you can; a more open hip trains the rectus femoris harder.
Start each rep from a deep knee bend and extend until your legs are straight.
Kneel on a soft surface with your knees hip-width apart and your hips straight.
Lean back as one piece from knees to head, only as far as you can return under control.
Pull yourself back up with your thighs without bending at the hips.
Hold on to something sturdy and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and lean back so knees, hips and shoulders stay in one line.
Lower as far as you can control, then straighten your knees to come back up.
Line up your knees with the machine's pivot and lock the thigh pad down firmly.
Sit tall or lean slightly forward so your hamstrings start in a stretch.
Curl your heels under the seat as far as you can, then return slowly to straight legs.
Lie face down with your knees just off the pad and the roller above your heels.
Keep your hips pressed into the bench as you curl.
Lower all the way to straight legs on every rep.
Kneel on a pad with your heels anchored under something solid.
Keep hips and torso in one line and lower yourself forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up just enough to restart.
Set the foot plate so your knees sit just behind the pad, and lock your heels in.
Start upright, then lower your torso forward under control by straightening your knees.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings while your hips stay extended.
Lie face down on a bench with your knees just past its end and a dumbbell held between your feet.
Curl your heels toward your glutes while your hips stay pressed into the bench.
Lower slowly to straight legs, and start light until the dumbbell feels secure between your feet.
Put an ankle strap on a low pulley and stand facing the machine, holding on for balance.
Curl your heel toward your glutes without letting your thigh swing forward.
Lower until the leg is straight, and finish all reps before you switch legs.
Lie face down with a band anchored low in front of you and looped around your heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes against the band.
Straighten your legs slowly while your hips stay on the floor.
Lie on your back with your heels on sliders or a towel on a smooth floor.
Lift your hips into a bridge and slide your heels out until your legs are almost straight.
Pull your heels back toward your glutes while your hips stay up.
Hold the bar with an underhand grip at about shoulder-width, elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up without swinging your torso or moving your elbows forward much.
Lower until your arms are fully straight before the next rep.
Stand with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells or one at a time, keeping your upper arms still.
Lower all the way down under control.
Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing each other.
Curl up with the thumbs leading and the elbows staying at your sides.
Lower to straight arms without swinging.
Sit back on a bench set to about 45–60 degrees and let your arms hang behind your torso.
Curl the dumbbells up without bringing your elbows forward.
Lower slowly into the full stretch at the bottom.
Stand on the band and hold the ends with palms facing forward.
Curl up to full elbow bend while your elbows stay at your sides.
Use a stronger band or stand on it wider when 30 reps become easy.
Sit at the preacher bench with your armpits snug against the top of the pad.
Lower the bar until your elbows are almost straight, slowing down near the bottom.
Curl up until your forearms are vertical without lifting your elbows off the pad.
Rest the back of your upper arm on a preacher pad or over the back of an upright incline bench.
Lower the dumbbell until your elbow is almost straight.
Curl it up without letting your shoulder roll forward or your elbow lift.
Face a low pulley holding a straight or EZ attachment with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle up while your elbows stay at your sides.
Lower until your arms are straight, keeping tension on the cable.
Set a pulley low, take one handle and step forward until the cable pulls your arm behind your torso.
Curl the handle forward and up while your upper arm stays behind your body.
Let your arm straighten fully behind you to stretch the biceps before the next rep.
Sit with your legs apart and brace the back of your upper arm against your inner thigh.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without moving your upper arm.
Lower until your arm is fully straight before the next rep.
Hold an EZ bar or barbell with an overhand grip at about shoulder-width.
Curl it up with straight wrists and your elbows at your sides.
Lower slowly to straight arms, using less weight than for a normal curl.
Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold it with your palms facing each other.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders, elbows fixed at your sides.
Lower until your arms are straight without letting the stack touch down.
Stand on the band and hold the ends with your palms facing each other.
Curl up with your elbows at your sides and your wrists straight.
Lower slowly against the band to straight arms.
Hold the rings with your palms up and lean back on straight arms, body in one line.
Curl your hands toward your forehead, pulling your body up while your elbows point forward.
Lower back to straight arms; walk your feet forward to make it harder.
Set the pulley high and hold a rope or bar with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push down until your arms are straight, spreading the rope ends at the bottom.
Let your forearms rise until they pass horizontal before the next rep.
Face away from a low or mid pulley with the rope behind your head and elbows pointing up.
Let your hands sink behind your head until your triceps are fully stretched.
Extend your elbows until your arms are straight, keeping your upper arms still.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands under the top plate, arms straight overhead.
Lower it behind your head until your elbows are fully bent, elbows pointing forward.
Press back to straight arms; sit with back support if your lower back arches.
Lie on a bench and hold the bar over your shoulders with a narrow grip.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind it.
Extend your arms fully without letting your elbows flare out.
Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms fully without letting your elbows drift out.
Sit upright with back support and hold the bar overhead with a narrow grip.
Lower it behind your head by bending your elbows while they keep pointing forward.
Extend back to straight arms without arching your lower back.
Hinge forward with a flat back and hold your upper arm alongside your torso.
Straighten your elbow until your arm is in line with your body.
Lower the dumbbell under control without letting your upper arm drop.
Hold a handle or the bare cable from a low pulley and hinge forward slightly.
Keep your upper arm against your side and extend the elbow until the arm is straight.
Let the forearm swing back to vertical under control.
Anchor the band high, for example over a pull-up bar, and hold it with your elbows at your sides.
Push down until your arms are straight, spreading your hands slightly at the bottom.
Let your forearms rise slowly to just above horizontal.
Anchor the band low behind you or stand on one end, holding the other end behind your head.
Point your elbows up and extend your arms overhead until they are straight.
Let your hands sink back behind your head slowly.
Hold a bar set at hip height or a pair of rings and lean in on straight arms, body in one line.
Bend your elbows to lower your forehead toward your hands while your elbows point forward.
Push back to straight arms; set the bar higher to make it easier.
Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the side until they are about level with your shoulders.
Lead with your elbows and lower slowly instead of letting the weights drop.
Set the pulley low and hold the handle with the hand farther from the machine.
Start with the hand in front of your hip so the side delt begins in a stretch.
Raise the arm out to shoulder height and lower under control.
Stand on the middle of a band and hold one end in each hand.
Raise your arms out to the side to shoulder height, elbows slightly bent.
Use a stronger band or a shorter grip once you can do 30 clean reps.
Hold a sturdy post with one hand and lean away from it with a dumbbell in the other hand.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is about parallel to the floor.
Lower it slowly until it hangs slightly across the front of your body before the next rep.
Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lead with your elbows and lift until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Stop lower if your shoulders complain, then lower the dumbbells under control.
Stand close to a low pulley holding a rope or bar with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull up along your body, elbows leading, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Stand on the middle of the band and hold the ends in front of your thighs.
Raise your elbows out and up until your hands reach chest height.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.
Rest your upper back on the bench edge with a padded bar over your hips.
Place your feet so your shins are vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels until your hips are fully extended, chin tucked and ribs down.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower until your hips nearly touch the floor.
Lie on your back with knees bent and heels about a foot from your hips.
Brace your abs and push through your heels until your hips are fully extended.
Hold the top for a second; add a weight on your hips or go single-leg when it gets easy.
Set the pad just below your hip crease so your hips can bend freely.
Hinge down from the hips with a neutral back until your hamstrings are stretched.
Come up until your body forms a straight line; do not arch past it.
Hold a plate or dumbbell against your chest to add load.
Sit with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Drive through your heels until your torso and thighs form a straight line.
Hold the top briefly with your ribs down, then lower until your hips nearly reach the seat.
Put a bench across the Smith machine and sit with your upper back against it, the padded bar over your hips.
Drive your hips up until thighs and torso are level, then turn the bar off the hooks.
Lower until your hips almost touch the floor and repeat with your chin tucked.
Sit with your upper back against a bench and hold one dumbbell on your hips.
Drive through your heels until your hips are level with your knees and shoulders.
Pause at the top, then lower under control.
Rest your upper back on a bench or couch with one foot planted and the other leg lifted.
Drive through the planted heel until your hips are level, without twisting.
Lower slowly and finish all reps before you switch legs.
Lie on your back with knees bent and a band stretched across your hips, ends held down by your hands.
Drive your hips up against the band until they line up with your knees and shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Lie face down on the pad with your hips at its edge and hold the handles.
Swing your legs up behind you until they line up with your torso, squeezing your glutes.
Lower your legs under control instead of letting the pendulum swing them.
Put an ankle strap on a low pulley and face the machine, holding on with both hands.
Lean forward slightly and push the working leg back until your hip is fully extended.
Return slowly until the knee comes in front of the hip, keeping your lower back still.
Sit with the pads on the outside of your knees and your back against the seat.
Push your knees apart as far as the machine allows and hold for a moment.
Let the pads come back together slowly.
Put an ankle strap on a low pulley and stand side-on with the strap on your far ankle.
Lift the leg out to the side without leaning your torso away.
Return slowly until the leg passes just in front of the standing foot.
Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with a band looped just above your knees.
Push your knees out against the band as far as you can.
Let them come back in slowly without losing tension.
Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent and the top leg straight in line with your body.
Raise the top leg toward the ceiling with your toes pointing forward, not up.
Lower slowly; add an ankle weight or a band once 20 reps get easy.
Sit with the pads on the inside of your knees, opened as wide as is comfortable.
Squeeze your knees together until the pads meet.
Return slowly into the stretch on every rep.
Put an ankle strap on a low pulley and stand side-on with the strap on your near ankle.
Start with the leg drawn out to the side, then sweep it across in front of your standing leg.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch along your inner thigh.
Lie on your side with your top leg resting on a bench at the knee or ankle and your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips and bottom leg until your body is straight, pressing the top leg into the bench.
Lower your hips toward the floor under control; resting the knee instead of the ankle makes it easier.
Anchor a band low to your side and loop it around the ankle nearest the anchor.
Step away until the band pulls your leg out, then sweep it across your body.
Let it return slowly while your hips stay square.
Stand on the edge of the step with your knees straight but not locked.
Lower your heels as far as they go and hold the stretch for a second.
Rise onto the balls of your feet; when the set gets hard, keep going in the bottom half.
Stand on one foot on a step and hold onto something for balance.
Let your heel sink below the step into a full stretch and pause there.
Rise as high as you can; hold a dumbbell in the free hand to add load.
Sit with the pad snug on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Drop your heels into a deep stretch and pause before each rep.
Press up as high as you can without bouncing out of the bottom.
Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a plate or step.
Rest the dumbbells on your knees and keep your knees bent at about 90 degrees.
Lower your heels fully, pause, then rise as high as you can.
Sit in the leg press with straight knees and the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Let the platform push your ankles into a deep stretch and hold it for a moment.
Press up through the balls of your feet as far as you can, with the safety catches within reach.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or a stack of plates, a dumbbell in each hand.
Lower your heels as far as they go and pause in the stretch.
Rise as high as you can on your toes with your knees straight.
Stand on the middle of the band, on a step if you have one, and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can with straight knees.
Lower your heels slowly below the step to stretch your calves.
Kneel facing a high pulley and hold the rope beside your head.
Curl your ribcage toward your pelvis by rounding your spine, not by bending at the hips.
Let your torso lengthen fully at the top before the next rep.
Hang from the bar with straight arms and stop any swing before you start.
Raise your knees or straight legs and curl your pelvis up toward your chest.
Lower slowly; start with bent knees and straighten them as you get stronger.
Lie on your back with knees bent and hands lightly at your temples or crossed on your chest.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by shortening the distance between ribs and pelvis.
Lower slowly; hold a plate on your chest to add load.
Lie on your back with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and arms on the floor.
Roll your hips up and toward your chest until your lower back leaves the floor.
Lower your hips slowly without letting your feet drop to the floor.
Stand tall with one dumbbell at your side and the other hand on your hip.
Lean toward the dumbbell side until you feel a stretch along the opposite side.
Pull yourself back upright with your obliques, then switch sides after the set.
Kneel behind a barbell loaded with round plates and hold it at shoulder-width.
Roll it forward slowly with your ribs pulled toward your hips, only as far as your lower back stays flat.
Pull the bar back to your knees by curling your trunk, not by bending at the hips.
Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Curl your torso up by rounding your spine, chin tucked, until you are nearly upright.
Lower slowly all the way back; hold a plate on your chest to add load.
Lie on your back with your hands under your hips and your legs straight.
Raise your legs until they point at the ceiling, then lift your hips slightly off the floor.
Lower your legs slowly without letting your lower back arch away from the floor.
Anchor a band high, kneel facing away from the anchor and hold the band beside your head.
Curl your ribcage toward your pelvis by rounding your back.
Return slowly until your torso is upright again.
Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and your knees raised.
Turn one shoulder toward the opposite knee as you straighten the other leg.
Switch sides in a slow, controlled rhythm and count one rep per side.
Set a pulley high, stand side-on and hold the handle with both hands above your far shoulder.
Pull it down and across your body to the opposite hip by turning your trunk.
Return under control and finish all reps before you turn around.
Stand side-on to a chest-high pulley and hold the handle against your breastbone.
Press it straight out in front of you and hold for two seconds without letting your torso turn.
Bring it back to your chest slowly; step further from the stack to make it harder.
Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on, holding the end against your chest.
Press your hands straight out and hold for two seconds while the band tries to twist you.
Return to your chest under control; move away from the anchor to add tension.
Stand side-on to a low pulley holding the handle in your near hand.
Let the cable pull you into a side bend toward it while your hips stay still.
Bend the other way past upright using the obliques on your far side.
Lie face down with your arms by your sides or reaching forward.
Lift your chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor by tightening your back and glutes.
Hold for a second at the top and lower slowly, keeping your neck in line with your spine.
Set the pulleys at shoulder height; with one cable, train one arm at a time.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows and open your arms until your chest is stretched.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Let the handles travel back until you feel a stretch, shoulders down and chest up.
Squeeze the handles together in front of you and return slowly.
Lie on a bench with the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch across your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together along the same arc while the elbow angle stays fixed.
Set the bench to about 30 degrees and start with the dumbbells above your upper chest.
Lower them in a wide arc with soft elbows until your chest is fully stretched.
Squeeze them back up and together without turning the movement into a press.
Set the pulleys low and stand between them, a handle in each hand with your arms down and slightly back.
Sweep your hands up and together in front of your upper chest with soft elbows.
Lower them along the same arc until your chest stretches; with one pulley, train one arm at a time.
Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand with your arms open wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging arc.
Open back up slowly until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Set the rings at about hip height and lean into them on straight arms, body in one line.
Let your arms open out to the sides as your chest lowers between the rings.
Pull your arms back together to return; stand more upright to make it easier.
Face the pad and set the handles so your arms start straight out in front.
Sweep your arms back in a wide arc until they are in line with your body.
Keep your chest on the pad and avoid shrugging as you pull.
Set a rope at upper-chest height or higher and hold it with thumbs pointing back.
Pull the rope toward your face, spreading the ends apart as your elbows go wide.
Finish with your hands beside your ears, then let the arms extend fully.
Hinge forward until your torso is nearly flat, or lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides with slightly bent elbows.
Stop when your arms are level with your back and lower under control.
Hold a band at shoulder height with straight arms and hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull the band apart until it touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly; move your hands closer together on the band to make it harder.
Set a pulley at shoulder height and hold the handle with the opposite hand, arm across your body.
Sweep your arm out and back in a wide arc until it is in line with your shoulders.
Let it return across your body slowly to stretch the rear delt.
Lie face down on a bench set to about 30 degrees with a light dumbbell in each hand.
Raise your arms out to the sides with soft elbows, leading with your knuckles.
Stop when your arms are in line with your body and lower slowly.
Anchor the band at face height and hold the ends with your palms facing down.
Pull toward your forehead, spreading your hands apart and turning your knuckles up.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
Hold the bar at arm's length with a shoulder-width grip; use straps if your grip fails first.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears without rolling them.
Hold the top briefly, then let your shoulders sink into a full stretch.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Shrug straight up as high as you can and pause.
Lower slowly until your shoulders are fully down.
Stand facing a low pulley and hold a straight bar with your arms hanging straight.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears and hold briefly.
Lower them as far as they go to stretch your traps.
Stand on the middle of the band and hold the ends at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up against the band and hold for a second.
Lower slowly until your shoulders hang fully down.
Set the bar at mid-thigh height and grip it just outside your hips.
Turn the bar off the hooks and shrug straight up, keeping your arms straight.
Lower until your shoulders are fully down, and hook the bar again after the set.
Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms up and wrists just past your knees.
Let the dumbbells roll down to your fingertips for a full stretch.
Curl your wrists up as far as they go without lifting your forearms.
Kneel beside a bench with your forearms on it, wrists just past the edge and palms up.
Let the bar roll down toward your fingertips, then curl it back up into your palms.
Curl your wrists up as far as they go without lifting your forearms off the bench.
Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms up, and the band anchored under your feet.
Curl your wrists up against the band as far as they go.
Lower slowly until your wrists are fully bent back.
Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms down and wrists past your knees.
Lift the back of your hands as high as you can, keeping your forearms still.
Lower slowly until your wrists are fully bent; light weights are enough.
Kneel beside a bench with your forearms on it, palms down and wrists just past the edge.
Raise the backs of your hands toward you as far as you can.
Lower slowly until your wrists are fully bent, using a light load.
Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms down, and the band anchored under your feet.
Lift the backs of your hands up against the band.
Lower slowly into a full stretch.

description.en: Two full-body sessions a week, each with a squat or hinge, a press, a pull and isolation work.
Three full-body sessions a week. Each muscle is trained on at least two days with a mix of compound and isolation work.
Four full-body sessions a week. Each muscle is trained on two or three days, with fewer exercises per session than an upper/lower split.
Two upper-body and two lower-body sessions a week, so every muscle is trained twice.
Five shorter full-body sessions a week. Each muscle is trained on two or three days, so no session has to carry much volume for one muscle.
Upper and lower days early in the week, then push, pull and legs, so every muscle is trained twice.
Push, pull and legs twice a week. The second rotation shifts the emphasis to other angles and sub-regions.
Three upper-body and three lower-body sessions a week. Shorter sessions than push/pull/legs, with each muscle trained two or three times.
Two sessions a week with squat, bench press and deadlift in each, one heavy and one lighter exposure per lift.
Squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, each lift undulating between heavy, light and moderate days.

name.en: Deadlift and light squat and bench

description.en: Four sessions with squat and deadlift twice and bench press three times a week, each with a heavy and a lighter exposure.
Five sessions with squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, plus accessory work for the upper back and arms.
Six shorter sessions with squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, for advanced lifters.
Two full-body sessions a week, each opening with heavy competition lifts and finishing with hypertrophy work.
Three full-body sessions a week: each competition lift twice, heavy and light, with hypertrophy work in every session.

name.en: Upper/lower with strength and hypertrophy days

description.en: An upper and a lower strength day built around the competition lifts, then an upper and a lower hypertrophy day.
An upper and a lower strength day around the competition lifts, then push, pull and legs days for hypertrophy.
Push, pull and legs twice a week: the first round built around heavy competition lifts, the second for hypertrophy.
